Post-review remediation round 10. On top of commit 7904d39 (round 9's barrier-before-delegation fix), Zainab round 10 (evidence/BIO-VIS-002/codex/SECURITY-REVIEW-ZAINAB-ROUND8.md) PASSed outright. Seyi round 10 (evidence/BIO-VIS-002/codex/REVIEW-Seyi-round9.md) FAILed on a further-refined version of the same F09 concern - again confirming the F08 PRODUCTION fix itself is correct (three rounds running now).

F09 continued: round 9's BarrierGatedVisitorCredentialAuditSink places the barrier immediately BEFORE delegating to the inner sink's CreateIfAbsentAsync. That only guarantees both callers reach the wrapper before EITHER enters the inner call - it does not control what happens after the barrier releases. The scheduler could still run caller A's entire inner create operation to completion before caller B's even starts, and the OLD defective ExistsAsync-then-WriteAsync sequence would ALSO pass under that exact serialized interleaving. The test still lacked the power to fail against the bug it was meant to catch.

This round is TEST-ONLY again - no production code moved (IVisitorCredentialAuditSink.cs/InMemoryVisitorCredentialAuditSink.cs/VisitorCredentialService.cs all untouched).

Fixed with a mutation/differential proof instead of a stronger barrier placement: AtomicFactoryRaceSink drives its own ConcurrentDictionary through the FACTORY-delegate overload of GetOrAdd with the barrier placed INSIDE the factory itself - under genuine contention .NET's documented contract allows the factory to be invoked on both racing threads before one result wins, so placing the barrier there forces exactly the 'both must observe absent before either write is permitted' sequence Seyi asked for. RacyCheckThenWriteSink deliberately reimplements the historical check-then-write bug (explicit absence check, shared barrier, then plain unconditional overwrite, with a semaphore pair forcing deterministic write ordering) so the SAME harness and assertions can be shown to fail against it - proving the test methodology itself has real discriminating power, not merely that the real implementation happens to behave. Two new tests exercise both reference sinks side by side. The two round-9 tests are kept as-is (still exercise the real production sink/service end-to-end, just with a weaker proof).

Honest scope of this proof (recorded in docs/features/bio-vis-002/README.md): it proves the test METHODOLOGY discriminates between an atomic and a non-atomic design under a genuinely forced concurrent sequence. It cannot force a mid-operation interleaving inside the real production InMemoryVisitorCredentialAuditSink itself, because GetOrAdd(TKey, TValue) is a single atomic step with no observable half-way point to barrier against. Combined with Seyi's own repeated source-inspection confirmation (three rounds running) that production CreateIfAbsentAsync is in fact the atomic design, this closes the loop without inventing a non-deterministic timing-based test against code that has no seam to hook.
